investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (409 Conflict)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T19:56:58Z with an identical 409 Conflict response from POST /api/agents. The swarm backend rejected the creation request with the message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", meaning the eval probe's service account or org has reached the maximum allowed swarm agent count and no new agents can be created. Because agent creation is the prerequisite for all downstream remote-agent checks, zero evidence was collected for any of the four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).
investigation.rootCause: The swarm backend enforces a hard per-org (or per-account) agent quota of 100. At the time the eval ran, that quota was already exhausted, causing POST /api/agents to return HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 808) failed immediately on this 409, no agent was created, no evidence was written, and all three remote-agents checks failed with the same error. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — Swarm agent quota exhausted for the eval probe's org: the 409 body explicitly states 'agent quota exceeded: limit is 100'. Leaked or un-cleaned agents from prior eval runs may have accumulated against the quota without being deleted by the withCleanup path (e.g., if previous runs crashed before cleanup executed).
SECONDARY — Eval probe service account or org is shared with non-eval workloads that have consumed the quota independently, leaving no headroom for the observability probe to create a new agent.

TERTIARY — A cleanup regression in the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) may have caused agents from prior runs to not be deleted, gradually filling the quota. The withCleanup wrapper seen at line 806 is the expected cleanup path; if it failed silently in prior runs, agents would accumulate.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint — production-api
investigations.summary: The AURA observability eval for check `image-generation-stream` (feature `media-generation`, runtime `production-api`) failed because the agent runtime returned a 404 on the session-open request, emitting a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame before any `generation_completed` frame or image URL could be produced. This is a localized eval infrastructure failure against the `production-api` runtime endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence, and the check is marked `required: false` with `statusImpact: informational`.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner (`infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs`, line 907) issued an SSE request to `/api/generate/image/stream` in the `production-api` runtime environment. The agent runtime responded with HTTP 404, which the stream translated into a `SESSION_OPEN_FAILED` error frame (evidence id: `failed-check.evidence`). Because the session could not be opened, no `generation_completed` frame was emitted and no image URL was returned, causing both required evidence keys (`frameTypes`, `imageUrlPresent`) to be absent (evidence id: `expected-output.missing-required-evidence`). The most likely cause is that the agent runtime harness targeted by the eval is either not deployed, deployed at a different URL than what `LOCAL_HARNESS_URL` / `SWARM_BASE_URL` resolves to, or is running an incompatible version that no longer exposes the expected endpoint path. The root cause is localized to the harness/runtime endpoint reachability for the `production-api` environment; it is not proven to be a user-facing outage.
